paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς ἦσαν πάντες ὁμοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: Kai en tō symplērousthai tēn hēmeran tēs pentēkostēs ēsan pantes homou epi to auto.

i18n.en: And when the day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all together in one place.

notes.official: The Pentecost opening at vv.1-4 integrates the Sinai-theophany imagery (Ex 19:16-19 thunder + cloud + shofar + fire) with the Num 11:24-30 Mosaic-spirit-distribution pattern. Pentecost (Greek *pentēkostē*) is the Greek name for the Jewish festival of Shavuot, the 50th day from Passover-Sabbath. In late-Second-Temple Judaism, Shavuot was associated both with the wheat-harvest first-fruits and with the Sinai-theophany / Torah-giving (rabbinic *zĕman mattan tôrāṯēnū* identification at Mekhilta Yitro 9; Jub 6:17-22). The Lukan choice of Pentecost as the spirit-outpouring timing is theologically-loaded: the event is framed as a Sinai-typological renewal. See central-glossary entry `pentecost-acts-2-tongues-of-fire-sinai-num-11-cross-corpus`.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἄφνω ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἦχος ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας καὶ ἐπλήρωσεν ὅλον τὸν οἶκον οὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι·
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto aphnō ek tou ouranou ēchos hōsper pheromenēs pnoēs biaias kai eplērōsen holon ton oikon hou ēsan kathēmenoi·

i18n.en: And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐφ’ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: kai ōphthēsan autois diamerizomenai glōssai hōsei pyros, kai ekathisen eph’ hena hekaston autōn,

i18n.en: And there appeared to them tongues being distributed, as of fire, and it sat upon each one of them,

notes.official: *diamerizomenai glōssai hōsei pyros* 'divided tongues as of fire'. The fire-and-tongue imagery integrates Sinai-theophany fire (Ex 19:18; 24:17 — the consuming fire on the mountain) with the rabbinic tradition (b. Šabbat 88b; Mekhilta Yitro) that at Sinai the divine-voice divided into 70 languages so all peoples could understand. The Acts 2:9-11 multinational audience-list at vv.9-11 functionally reactivates the Sinai-as-Torah-to-all-nations tradition.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις καθὼς τὸ πνεῦμα ἐδίδου ἀποφθέγγεσθαι αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai eplēsthēsan pantes pneumatos hagiou, kai ērxanto lalein heterais glōssais kathōs to pneuma edidou apophthengesthai autois.

i18n.en: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.

notes.official: *ērxanto lalein heterais glōssais* 'they began to speak in other tongues'. The Lukan-Acts *heterais glōssais* ambiguity preserves both possible readings: xenoglossia (actual human-languages, supported by the vv.9-11 multinational audience list) vs glossolalia (ecstatic-spirit-language, as 1 Cor 12-14 develops). Both readings have textual warrant; the WoH-Translation does not adjudicate.

paragraphs.text: Ἦσαν δὲ εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι, ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν·
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de eis Ierousalēm katoikountes Ioudaioi, andres eulabeis apo pantos ethnous tōn hypo ton ouranon·

i18n.en: Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem Jews, devout men, from every nation under heaven.

paragraphs.text: γενομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης συνῆλθε τὸ πλῆθος καὶ συνεχύθη, ὅτι ἤκουον εἷς ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ λαλούντων αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: genomenēs de tēs phōnēs tautēs synēlthe to plēthos kai synechythē, hoti ēkouon heis hekastos tē idia dialektō lalountōn autōn.

i18n.en: And when this sound occurred, the multitude came together and was bewildered, because each one was hearing them speak in his own language.

paragraphs.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον λέγοντες· Οὐχ ἰδοὺ πάντες οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ λαλοῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι;
paragraphs.translit: existanto de kai ethaumazon legontes· Ouch idou pantes houtoi eisin hoi lalountes Galilaioi?

i18n.en: And they were amazed and marveled, saying: "Behold, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?

paragraphs.text: καὶ πῶς ἡμεῖς ἀκούομεν ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ ἡμῶν ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθημεν;
paragraphs.translit: kai pōs hēmeis akouomen hekastos tē idia dialektō hēmōn en hē egennēthēmen?

i18n.en: And how is it that we each hear in our own native language?

paragraphs.text: Πάρθοι καὶ Μῆδοι καὶ Ἐλαμῖται, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν, Ἰουδαίαν τε καὶ Καππαδοκίαν, Πόντον καὶ τὴν Ἀσίαν,
paragraphs.translit: Parthoi kai Mēdoi kai Elamitai, kai hoi katoikountes tēn Mesopotamian, Ioudaian te kai Kappadokian, Ponton kai tēn Asian,

i18n.en: Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those dwelling in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,

notes.official: The vv.9-11 multinational audience list (Parthians + Medes + Elamites + Mesopotamian-Judean-Cappadocian-Pontic-Asian + Phrygian-Pamphylian + Egyptian-Libyan + Roman + Cretan-Arabian) has been variously interpreted: an ecumenical-extent list, an astrological-zodiacal list (Hellenistic conventions), an order-following Jewish-diaspora-major-centers, or a tradition-bound list of the 70 nations of Gen 10. The Lukan-Acts framing is on the universal-extent of the apostolic mission. The 70-nations / Gen 10 background reinforces the Sinai-typological framing (the rabbinic tradition's 70-languages-at-Sinai).

paragraphs.text: Φρυγίαν τε καὶ Παμφυλίαν, Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς Λιβύης τῆς κατὰ Κυρήνην, καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες Ῥωμαῖοι,
paragraphs.translit: Phrygian te kai Pamphylian, Aigypton kai ta merē tēs Libyēs tēs kata Kyrēnēn, kai hoi epidēmountes Rhōmaioi,

i18n.en: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and the visiting Romans,

paragraphs.text: Ἰουδαῖοί τε καὶ προσήλυτοι, Κρῆτες καὶ Ἄραβες, ἀκούομεν λαλούντων αὐτῶν ταῖς ἡμετέραις γλώσσαις τὰ μεγαλεῖα τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Ioudaioi te kai prosēlytoi, Krētes kai Arabes, akouomen lalountōn autōn tais hēmeterais glōssais ta megaleia tou theou.

i18n.en: both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs — we hear them speaking in our own languages the mighty works of God."

paragraphs.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες καὶ διηπόρουν, ἄλλος πρὸς ἄλλον λέγοντες· Τί θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι;
paragraphs.translit: existanto de pantes kai diēporoun, allos pros allon legontes· Ti thelei touto einai?

i18n.en: And all were amazed and perplexed, saying to one another: "What does this mean?"

paragraphs.text: ἕτεροι δὲ διαχλευάζοντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Γλεύκους μεμεστωμένοι εἰσίν.
paragraphs.translit: heteroi de diachleuazontes elegon hoti Gleukous memestōmenoi eisin.

i18n.en: But others, mocking, said: "They are filled with new wine."

paragraphs.text: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος σὺν τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐπῆρεν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπεφθέγξατο αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Ἰερουσαλὴμ πάντες, τοῦτο ὑμῖν γνωστὸν ἔστω καὶ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μου.
paragraphs.translit: Statheis de ho Petros syn tois hendeka epēren tēn phōnēn autou kai apephthenxato autois· Andres Ioudaioi kai hoi katoikountes Ierousalēm pantes, touto hymin gnōston estō kai enōtisasthe ta rhēmata mou.

i18n.en: But Peter, standing up with the eleven, lifted up his voice and addressed them: "Men of Judea and all who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.

paragraphs.text: οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὑμεῖς ὑπολαμβάνετε οὗτοι μεθύουσιν, ἔστιν γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας,
paragraphs.translit: ou gar hōs hymeis hypolambanete houtoi methyousin, estin gar hōra tritē tēs hēmeras,

i18n.en: For these are not drunk, as you suppose, since it is only the third hour of the day.

paragraphs.text: ἀλλὰ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Ἰωήλ·
paragraphs.translit: alla touto estin to eirēmenon dia tou prophētou Iōēl·

i18n.en: But this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:

notes.official: Peter's sermon centerpiece — the Joel 2:28-32 LXX (= MT Joel 3:1-5) citation at vv.17-21. The longest extended OT-citation in Acts and the explanatory framework for the Pentecost event. The citation deploys Joel as the explanatory-framework: the Spirit-outpouring inaugurates 'the last days', and the cosmic-signs are the eschatological-confirmation of the day-of-the-Lord context.

paragraphs.text: Καὶ ἔσται ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, λέγει ὁ θεός, ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες ὑμῶν, καὶ οἱ νεανίσκοι ὑμῶν ὁράσεις ὄψονται, καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὑμῶν ἐνύπνια ἐνυπνιασθήσονται·
paragraphs.translit: Kai estai en tais eschatais hēmerais, legei ho theos, ekcheō apo tou pneumatos mou epi pasan sarka, kai prophēteusousin hoi huioi hymōn kai hai thygateres hymōn, kai hoi neaniskoi hymōn horaseis opsontai, kai hoi presbyteroi hymōn enypnia enypniasthēsontai·

i18n.en: "And it shall be in the last days, says God, I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.

notes.official: Peter substitutes *en tais eschatais hēmerais* 'in the last days' for Joel's *meta tauta* 'after these things' — a redactional adjustment that re-temporalizes Joel's prophecy as an inaugurated-eschatology statement. The substitution is one of the most-discussed Lukan-Acts editorial adjustments and is preserved in NA28/UBS5 critical text.

paragraphs.text: καί γε ἐπὶ τοὺς δούλους μου καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς δούλας μου ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ge epi tous doulous mou kai epi tas doulas mou en tais hēmerais ekeinais ekcheō apo tou pneumatos mou, kai prophēteusousin.

i18n.en: Yes, and on my menservants and on my maidservants in those days I will pour out from my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.

paragraphs.text: καὶ δώσω τέρατα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ σημεῖα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κάτω, αἷμα καὶ πῦρ καὶ ἀτμίδα καπνοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: kai dōsō terata en tō ouranō anō kai sēmeia epi tēs gēs katō, haima kai pyr kai atmida kapnou·

i18n.en: And I will show wonders in the heaven above and signs on the earth below — blood and fire and vapor of smoke.

notes.official: **COSMIC-SIGNS CITATION (Joel 2:30-31 / 3:3-4 LXX).** *terata en tō ouranō anō kai sēmeia epi tēs gēs katō, haima kai pyr kai atmida kapnou* 'wonders in the heaven above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke'. Cross-corpus chain: Joel 2:30-31 → Mk 13:24-25 // Mt 24:29 → Lk 21:25-26 → Rev 6:12-13. The cosmic-signs cluster is one of the most-systematic NT redeployments of the Hebrew Bible prophetic-apocalyptic substrate. Documented at the central-glossary entry `cosmic-signs-cluster-joel-2-mark-13-acts-2-luke-21-rev-6-cross-corpus`. Bidirectional cross-corpus with v2.60.0 Qur'an `inshiqaq-al-qamar-splitting-of-the-moon-sura-54-1`.

paragraphs.text: ὁ ἥλιος μεταστραφήσεται εἰς σκότος καὶ ἡ σελήνη εἰς αἷμα πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ἡμέραν κυρίου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐπιφανῆ.
paragraphs.translit: ho hēlios metastraphēsetai eis skotos kai hē selēnē eis haima prin elthein hēmeran kyriou tēn megalēn kai epiphanē.

i18n.en: The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.

paragraphs.text: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὃς ἂν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: kai estai pas hos an epikalesētai to onoma kyriou sōthēsetai.

i18n.en: And it shall be that whoever calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved."

paragraphs.text: Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους τούτους. Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον, ἄνδρα ἀποδεδειγμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς δυνάμεσι καὶ τέρασι καὶ σημείοις οἷς ἐποίησεν δι’ αὐτοῦ ὁ θεὸς ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν, καθὼς αὐτοὶ οἴδατε,
paragraphs.translit: Andres Israēlitai, akousate tous logous toutous. Iēsoun ton Nazōraion, andra apodedeigmenon apo tou theou eis hymas dynamesi kai terasi kai sēmeiois hois epoiēsen di’ autou ho theos en mesō hymōn, kathōs autoi oidate,

i18n.en: "Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus of Nazareth, a man attested to you by God with mighty works and wonders and signs that God did through him in your midst, as you yourselves know —

notes.official: Peter's kerygmatic sermon centerpiece engages two major HB citations — Ps 16:8-11 LXX (vv.25-28, the not-abandoned-to-Hades + not-seeing-corruption Davidic typology) and Ps 110:1 LXX (vv.34-35, the right-hand-of-the-Lord enthronement). Both psalms are read messianically with Davidic-typological backing: David died and was buried, his tomb is still with you (v.29) — but the Risen Christ is the David-typological-fulfillment.

paragraphs.text: τοῦτον τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βουλῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ ἔκδοτον διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμων προσπήξαντες ἀνείλατε,
paragraphs.translit: touton tē hōrismenē boulē kai prognōsei tou theou ekdoton dia cheiros anomōn prospēxantes aneilate,

i18n.en: this man, delivered up by the determined purpose and foreknowledge of God, you crucified and killed by the hands of lawless men.

paragraphs.text: ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἀνέστησεν λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου, καθότι οὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hon ho theos anestēsen lysas tas ōdinas tou thanatou, kathoti ouk ēn dynaton krateisthai auton hyp’ autou·

i18n.en: Him God raised up, having loosed the pangs of death, because it was not possible that he should be held by it.

paragraphs.text: Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς αὐτόν· Προορώμην τὸν κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός, ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ.
paragraphs.translit: Dauid gar legei eis auton· Proorōmēn ton kyrion enōpion mou dia pantos, hoti ek dexiōn mou estin hina mē saleuthō.

i18n.en: For David says concerning him: "I saw the Lord always before me, for he is at my right hand, so that I shall not be shaken.

paragraphs.text: διὰ τοῦτο ηὐφράνθη ἡ καρδία μου καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μου, ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἡ σάρξ μου κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι·
paragraphs.translit: dia touto ēuphranthē hē kardia mou kai ēgalliasato hē glōssa mou, eti de kai hē sarx mou kataskēnōsei ep’ elpidi·

i18n.en: Therefore my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced; moreover my flesh also shall dwell in hope,

paragraphs.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μου εἰς ᾅδην, οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.
paragraphs.translit: hoti ouk enkataleipseis tēn psychēn mou eis hadēn, oude dōseis ton hosion sou idein diaphthoran.

i18n.en: because you will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will you allow your Holy One to see corruption.

paragraphs.text: ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδοὺς ζωῆς, πληρώσεις με εὐφροσύνης μετὰ τοῦ προσώπου σου.
paragraphs.translit: egnōrisas moi hodous zōēs, plērōseis me euphrosynēs meta tou prosōpou sou.

i18n.en: You have made known to me the ways of life; you will fill me with gladness in your presence."

paragraphs.text: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐξὸν εἰπεῖν μετὰ παρρησίας πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ τοῦ πατριάρχου Δαυίδ, ὅτι καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ ἐτάφη καὶ τὸ μνῆμα αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης·
paragraphs.translit: Andres adelphoi, exon eipein meta parrēsias pros hymas peri tou patriarchou Dauid, hoti kai eteleutēsen kai etaphē kai to mnēma autou estin en hēmin achri tēs hēmeras tautēs·

i18n.en: Brothers, I may say to you with confidence concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day.

paragraphs.text: προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων, καὶ εἰδὼς ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: prophētēs oun hyparchōn, kai eidōs hoti horkō ōmosen autō ho theos ek karpou tēs osphyos autou kathisai epi ton thronon autou,

i18n.en: Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath that one of the fruit of his loins would sit upon his throne,

paragraphs.text: προϊδὼν ἐλάλησεν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ χριστοῦ ὅτι οὔτε ἐγκατελείφθη εἰς ᾅδην οὔτε ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.
paragraphs.translit: proidōn elalēsen peri tēs anastaseōs tou christou hoti oute enkateleiphthē eis hadēn oute hē sarx autou eiden diaphthoran.

i18n.en: he foresaw and spoke of the resurrection of the Christ, that he was neither abandoned to Hades nor did his flesh see corruption.

paragraphs.text: τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνέστησεν ὁ θεός, οὗ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες.
paragraphs.translit: touton ton Iēsoun anestēsen ho theos, hou pantes hēmeis esmen martyres.

i18n.en: This Jesus God raised up, and of that we all are witnesses.

paragraphs.text: τῇ δεξιᾷ οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑψωθεὶς τήν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐξέχεεν τοῦτο ὃ ὑμεῖς καὶ βλέπετε καὶ ἀκούετε.
paragraphs.translit: tē dexia oun tou theou hypsōtheis tēn te epangelian tou pneumatos tou hagiou labōn para tou patros execheen touto ho hymeis kai blepete kai akouete.

i18n.en: Therefore, being exalted to the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this which you both see and hear.

paragraphs.text: οὐ γὰρ Δαυὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, λέγει δὲ αὐτός· Εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου,
paragraphs.translit: ou gar Dauid anebē eis tous ouranous, legei de autos· Eipen ho kyrios tō kyriō mou· Kathou ek dexiōn mou,

i18n.en: For David did not ascend into the heavens, but he himself says: "The Lord said to my Lord, 'Sit at my right hand,

paragraphs.text: ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
paragraphs.translit: heōs an thō tous echthrous sou hypopodion tōn podōn sou.

i18n.en: until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.'"

paragraphs.text: ἀσφαλῶς οὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι καὶ κύριον αὐτὸν καὶ χριστὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός, τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε.
paragraphs.translit: asphalōs oun ginōsketō pas oikos Israēl hoti kai kyrion auton kai christon epoiēsen ho theos, touton ton Iēsoun hon hymeis estaurōsate.

i18n.en: Therefore let all the house of Israel know with certainty that God has made him both Lord and Christ — this Jesus whom you crucified."

paragraphs.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ κατενύγησαν τὴν καρδίαν, εἶπόν τε πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀποστόλους· Τί ποιήσωμεν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί;
paragraphs.translit: Akousantes de katenygēsan tēn kardian, eipon te pros ton Petron kai tous loipous apostolous· Ti poiēsōmen, andres adelphoi?

i18n.en: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles: "Brothers, what shall we do?"

paragraphs.text: Πέτρος δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Μετανοήσατε, καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ εἰς ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ὑμῶν, καὶ λήμψεσθε τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος·
paragraphs.translit: Petros de pros autous· Metanoēsate, kai baptisthētō hekastos hymōn epi tō onomati Iēsou christou eis aphesin tōn hamartiōn hymōn, kai lēmpsesthe tēn dōrean tou hagiou pneumatos·

i18n.en: And Peter said to them: "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

notes.official: *baptisthētō ... epi tō onomati Iēsou christou* 'let each be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ'. The Acts-distinctive baptismal formula 'in the name of Jesus Christ' (cf. Acts 8:16; 10:48; 19:5) is structurally different from the Mt 28:19 triadic-formula 'in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit'. Modern scholarship widely accepts that the Acts formula reflects the earliest baptismal practice (cf. the Mt 28:19 Conybeare-hypothesis discussion at the existing central entry `great-commission-mt-28-19-20-trinitarian-baptismal-formula-conybeare-hypothesis-cross-corpus-with-disavowals`). The Acts pattern is documented as a structurally-distinct baptismal convention without theological-pre-resolution of the Trinitarian-vs-Christo-monotheistic dispute.

paragraphs.text: ὑμῖν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς εἰς μακράν, ὅσους ἂν προσκαλέσηται κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν.
paragraphs.translit: hymin gar estin hē epangelia kai tois teknois hymōn kai pasi tois eis makran, hosous an proskalesētai kyrios ho theos hēmōn.

i18n.en: For the promise is to you and to your children and to all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God shall call to himself."

paragraphs.text: ἑτέροις τε λόγοις πλείοσιν διεμαρτύρατο, καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτοὺς λέγων· Σώθητε ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς τῆς σκολιᾶς ταύτης.
paragraphs.translit: heterois te logois pleiosin diemartyrato, kai parekalei autous legōn· Sōthēte apo tēs geneas tēs skolias tautēs.

i18n.en: And with many other words he testified and exhorted them, saying: "Be saved from this crooked generation."

paragraphs.text: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀποδεξάμενοι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθησαν, καὶ προσετέθησαν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ψυχαὶ ὡσεὶ τρισχίλιαι.
paragraphs.translit: hoi men oun apodexamenoi ton logon autou ebaptisthēsan, kai prosetethēsan en tē hēmera ekeinē psychai hōsei trischiliai.

i18n.en: So then, those who received his word were baptized, and there were added that day about three thousand souls.

paragraphs.text: ἦσαν δὲ προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ, τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς.
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de proskarterountes tē didachē tōn apostolōn kai tē koinōnia, tē klasei tou artou kai tais proseuchais.

i18n.en: And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.

paragraphs.text: ἐγίνετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος, πολλά τε τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο.
paragraphs.translit: egineto de pasē psychē phobos, polla te terata kai sēmeia dia tōn apostolōn egineto.

i18n.en: And awe came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles.

paragraphs.text: πάντες δὲ οἱ πιστεύοντες ἦσαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά,
paragraphs.translit: pantes de hoi pisteuontes ēsan epi to auto kai eichon hapanta koina,

i18n.en: And all who believed were together and had all things in common,

paragraphs.text: καὶ τὰ κτήματα καὶ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον καὶ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσιν καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ta ktēmata kai tas hyparxeis epipraskon kai diemerizon auta pasin kathoti an tis chreian eichen·

i18n.en: and they were selling their possessions and goods and distributing them to all, as anyone had need.

paragraphs.text: καθ’ ἡμέραν τε προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, κλῶντές τε κατ’ οἶκον ἄρτον, μετελάμβανον τροφῆς ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ ἀφελότητι καρδίας,
paragraphs.translit: kath’ hēmeran te proskarterountes homothymadon en tō hierō, klōntes te kat’ oikon arton, metelambanon trophēs en agalliasei kai aphelotēti kardias,

i18n.en: And day by day, continuing with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they were partaking of food with gladness and simplicity of heart,

paragraphs.text: αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαόν. ὁ δὲ κύριος προσετίθει τοὺς σῳζομένους καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.
paragraphs.translit: ainountes ton theon kai echontes charin pros holon ton laon. ho de kyrios prosetithei tous sōzomenous kath’ hēmera epi to auto.

i18n.en: praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord was adding to their number day by day those who were being saved.
